summary: Spokane reservation steel tower built 1964 to replace a lookout four miles north; staffed each fire season and still in use.

facts.design: 53 ft steel tower with live-in cab

access.note: On the Spokane Indian Reservation, administered by the reservation. The sources read do not describe visitor rules; ask the tribal administration before any visit.

visit.trail_note: TrailChick reports a road of about 3 miles to the summit; a high-clearance 4WD may be needed depending on the season.

events.note: 53 ft steel tower with live-in cab; replaced the Spokane Mountain lookout four miles to the north

Site change discussed: the original survey planned the tower for Spokane Butte; a December 1962 reply proposed Wellpinit Mountain with a 40-foot cabin tower, citing electric service and better reservation coverage; TrailChick says the Colville suggested the site for wider views and electrical service
The lookout called in the Line Fire
The Sherwood Fire, started from a lightning storm, came within a mile or two of the lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 53 ft. TrailChick's page header says 54' but its text says 53'. The story and facts use 53 ft (16.2 m, converted).

TrailChick gives 1933 as the site established date; the register and firelookout.com date the current structure to 1964. The sources do not say what stood on the summit before 1964, so both dates are recorded and the story reports the difference.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1964 and the Spokane Mountain replacement agree across the register and firelookout.com. Elevation is unresolved: the record's 1021.1 m matches the register's 3,350 ft, but TrailChick gives 3,464 ft and firelookout.com gives 3413 ft; the record was left unchanged for a human to check the datum. The access level 'permission' is not stated by any source read; it reflects tribal administration and should be confirmed with the Spokane tribal administration. The staffing 'as_of' 2024 is taken from TrailChick's last-updated date (March 24, 2024). The 1962 letters are quoted on a lookout-history site, not from an archive; the 40-foot tower was only a proposal and the built tower is 53 ft. The reasons for the site change (electric service, reservation coverage, wider views) are sourced to the December 1962 letter and TrailChick, and the story now states them.
